scope.heading: Scope
scope.body: This statement covers the popyplan-panel web panel (this site, served under this same domain) and the Popyplan mobile app (iOS and Android). It does not cover embedded third-party content (for example, images or documents uploaded by an entity) or sites linked outside these two products.

status.heading: Compliance status
status.body: This site is partially compliant with level AA of the UNE-EN 301549:2022 Standard (WCAG 2.1), due to the exceptions described in «Non-accessible content». It will become «fully compliant» once the automatic audit (axe) and manual keyboard tests cover every page without documented exceptions (Phase 6, task W5 of this panel).

nonAccessible.heading: Non-accessible content
nonAccessible.intro: As of this statement, the following panel pages don't yet have a dedicated automatic accessibility test (axe) — the coverage chosen so far is representative of the three areas and the shared patterns (tables, dialogs with focus trapping, charts, forms), but not exhaustive:
nonAccessible.list: Communities, Activities, Reports, On-call, Settings, Announcements, Surveys and Resources of the entity panel; Reports of the umbrella entity panel; and Audit log, Help, Verifications, Roles, Reports, Metrics and entity record of the platform panel. Extending this coverage is mechanical work, documented in CLAUDE.md («Accessibility»).

preparation.heading: Preparation of this statement
preparation.body: This statement was prepared on September 5, 2026. It was reviewed through automatic evaluation (axe-core on the pages with a dedicated test, see «Non-accessible content») and manual keyboard and screen reader review of the main flows across the panel's three areas.

contact.heading: Feedback and contact details
contact.body: You can report any accessibility problem, or request information in an accessible format, by writing to <email>{contactEmail}</email>.

procedure.heading: Enforcement procedure
procedure.body: If after contacting us you don't get a response or aren't satisfied with it, you can file a complaint under article 13 of <rd>Royal Decree 1112/2018</rd>.

inicio.title: Home
inicio.summary: Overview of your entity for today: today's activities, pending alerts, active programs and this month's metrics.
inicio.details: Everything on Home is already computed by the platform: today's activities, pending help alerts and reports (counts only), this month's metrics and active programs. The on-call counters are hidden — not shown as an error — for roles the backend doesn't let moderate (analyst, facilitator, referent); they simply don't see those cards. A counter that fails for any other reason shows as unavailable rather than as zero.
actions: See how many help alerts and reports are pending (only whoever moderates or is on call)
Check people, activities and attendance for the month
tips: Counters are counts, not lists: open the section to see the actual items.
Home metrics follow the same <5 privacy rule as the rest of the panel.

personas.title: People
personas.summary: The people who take part in your entity, with their communities, recent activity and referent. Never shows contact details: Popyplan works with aliases.
personas.details: The list mixes active people and, if you tick 'include invited', pending invitations — an invited row has no profile yet, so communities and attendance show as '—'. People are always added by invitation email: the panel never creates accounts and never shows contact details. Importing a file always runs a dry-run preview first; rows with errors are reported per row but don't block confirming the valid ones.
actions: Search and filter by community, referent or join date
Invite a person or import an Excel/CSV (owner and moderator)
Include pending invitations and resend or revoke them
tips: Filter by community or referent before searching by name — it's faster on long lists.
A 'already a member' error means that email belongs to an active member.

personaFicha.title: Person profile
personaFicha.summary: Summary of a person's participation in your entity: communities, activities for the period and next activity. No email, phone or notes: the relationship always goes through the app.
personaFicha.details: The profile shows only participation in your entity: communities, activities for the period with their attendance status, and the next activity. It never shows email, phone, documents or free-text notes — the relationship goes through the app chat. The support-network section appears only for that person's referent; anyone else, including the owner, doesn't see the section at all. A referent without a reference to that person sees a 'no access' state instead of the profile.
actions: Assign or change their referent (owner and moderator)
See their support network (only their referent)
Review which activities they signed up for and whether they attended
tips: Only the assigned referent sees the support network — don't look for it as owner.
The activity period on the profile is the current month, like the People list.
personaFicha.audience: Owner, moderator and that person's referent.

comunidades.title: Communities
comunidades.summary: Your entity's communities and their members: who belongs, who moderates, visibility and pending join requests.
comunidades.details: Communities belong to the entity and each keeps its own visibility (open, on request or private). Join requests wait here until someone accepts them, and removing a member always asks for confirmation first. Families communities live in their own separate space — they never mix with members' communities unless you explicitly enable cross-space viewing from the Families section.
actions: See each community, its visibility and its members
Appoint moderators or remove someone (owner and moderator)
tips: Rejecting a request is reversible — the person can ask to join again.

actividades.title: Activities
actividades.summary: The period's activities with their sign-ups, attendees and organiser. Includes upcoming activities when the period reaches the future.
actividades.details: The list covers the period you choose, including upcoming activities. The organiser column is only filled if your role can see the nominal list; otherwise it shows '—' rather than a guessed name. Opening the attendance sheet is only offered when the Attendance section is in your menu — a referent sees the activities but no attendance link. Counters per row are sign-ups, attended and not attended for the period. When creating or editing an activity you can set an optional level (beginner, intermediate or advanced); without it, the activity is for all levels.
actions: See who is responsible for each one
tips: Extend the period to see upcoming activities, not just past ones.

asistencia.title: Attendance
asistencia.summary: Choose an activity to take attendance or do the QR check-in.
asistencia.details: Attendance is always per activity: pick one from the list to open its attendance sheet. The list shows the period's activities with their status, so you can jump straight to the one that just finished or starts soon. The same screen is the Activities section itself — the list is the selector, there is no separate attendance overview.
actions: Mark attendance by hand or scan the app's QR code
tips: Marking by hand only works once the activity has started.

asistenciaEvento.title: Attendance list
asistenciaEvento.summary: Who signed up for this activity and who has shown up. QR check-in only works from two hours before to twelve hours after the start.
asistenciaEvento.details: Marking attendance by hand is only possible once the activity has started. QR check-in accepts the token pasted from the app or the full 'popyplan://checkin/…' link, and can scan with the camera where the browser supports it. It works from two hours before to twelve hours after the start; outside that window the backend's own message is shown. A repeat check-in shows as a notice, not an error — nothing breaks.
actions: Mark each person as “attended” or “did not attend”
Scan the QR code shown in the person's app or paste their code
tips: No camera? Paste the popyplan:// link from any message and the token is extracted.
A second scan of the same code shows 'already checked in' — the count stays at one.

comunicaciones.title: Announcements
comunicaciones.summary: Official announcements from the entity to all members, to a community or to the families space, with their history and number of recipients.
comunicaciones.details: Announcements are official entity messages to all members, one community or the families space — the families option only unlocks once a families community exists. There is no recipient preview: the confirmation describes the audience and the real recipient count appears after sending. The support-network welcome template only fills the form; sending is always your decision, and overwriting an existing draft asks for confirmation first.
actions: Draft and send an announcement (owner and moderator)
Use the welcome-to-the-support-network template once the families space exists
tips: The recipient count in the history is the real number reached — check it after sending.
The template overwrites the current draft; cancel if you want to keep your text.

encuestas.title: Surveys
encuestas.summary: Anonymous, aggregated surveys: the periodic ones you create and the ones the app sends on its own after each activity.
encuestas.details: Only periodic surveys are created here; the app sends post-activity surveys on its own after each completed activity, so they appear in the list without anyone creating them. Open or closed status comes from the survey's own start and end dates. All responses are anonymous and aggregated — no answer is ever linked to a person, and any result with fewer than five responses hides its detail.
actions: Create a periodic survey with its questions (owner and moderator)
See whether it's open or closed and open its results
tips: Post-activity surveys are created by the app — don't look for a 'new post-event survey' button.

encuestaResultados.title: Survey results
encuestaResultados.summary: Aggregated results per question. With fewer than five responses the detail isn't shown, so no one can be identified.
encuestaResultados.details: Results are aggregated per question: average and distribution for rating questions, an unordered list for short text — text answers have no author and no order. Any question with fewer than five responses is suppressed and shown as <5, so no one can be worked out from the numbers. The anonymity notice is always on screen because it is the rule, not a detail.
actions: See each question's average and distribution
Read text answers with no order or author
tips: <5 means 'fewer than five responses', not zero — the survey may still be open.

biblioteca.title: Library
biblioteca.summary: The entity's content library: text, PDFs, videos, audio and links, organised by category and aimed at members, families or anyone.
biblioteca.details: Resources are grouped by category — help, training, families, habits, activities, about, and 'How to support' for the support network — and each has an audience: members, families or anyone. The families audience only appears once a families community exists. Files are validated before upload (20 MB and common document, audio or video formats) and the server validates again anyway, so a rejected file is explained with the backend's message.
actions: Create, edit or delete resources (owner and moderator)
Choose category and audience; “How to support” is the category for the support network
tips: Editing keeps the existing file unless you pick a new one — the file field starts empty.
Deleting a resource always asks for confirmation and cannot be undone.

familias.title: Families
familias.summary: The entity's families space, separate from the members' space: its communities, upcoming activities, announcements and resources, and the aggregated support-network counters. Nobody declares being family to anyone.
familias.details: The families space is separate from the members' space and the two only mix if you allow cross-space viewing per community — the confirmation explains the separation rule first. Counters follow the same privacy rule as the rest of the panel: any count under five distinct people shows as <5. Supporters waiting for a families community to exist are counted as people, and the panel tells you when creating one would welcome them in.
actions: Create the families community (owner and moderator)
Turn each community's cross-space viewing on or off
See how many people have a support network and how many supporters are waiting for the community to exist
tips: The separation banner is the rule, not a warning: members and families don't see each other.
Facilitators can see this section but only owner and moderator can create or change communities.

programas.title: Programs
programas.summary: Campaigns with fixed dates and a declared budget, with their aggregated final report. A program never lists people.
programas.details: A program is a campaign with closed dates and a declared budget, and its status only moves forward: draft → active → closed. A closed program cannot be edited again, and closing asks for closing notes. The report only contains aggregates — a program never lists people, not even for the owner. Metrics on a program's page are computed for the program's own date range.
actions: Create, activate and close programs (owner and moderator)
Download the CSV or PDF report (owner, moderator and analyst)
tips: Closing is irreversible — review the closing notes before confirming.

programaFicha.title: Program profile
programaFicha.summary: The program's status, dates, budget and metrics for its period, with its final report.
programaFicha.details: The profile shows the program's status, dates, budget and metrics computed for its own date range. Editing is only possible before closing: closing asks for notes and is irreversible. If the backend rejects a date change, its exact validation message is shown instead of a generic one. The report downloads as CSV or PDF and contains only aggregates — never a list of people.
actions: Edit, activate or close the program with closing notes (owner and moderator)
tips: The page refreshes on its own after activate, close or edit — no manual reload needed.
programaFicha.audience: All entity roles; only the owner and moderator can manage it.

reportes.title: Reports
reportes.summary: Your entity's moderation report queue: what was reported, why and its current status.
reportes.details: The queue holds reports about content in your entity, with the reason and current status. You can assign a report to a team member, resolve it with a decision, or escalate it to Popyplan when it's beyond the entity — escalated reports also appear in the platform's global queue. Resolution and assignment are moderation decisions recorded in the report's history, along with who made them.
actions: Assign it, resolve it or escalate it to the platform
tips: Escalate when the content breaks platform rules, not just entity rules.

reporteDetalle.title: Report detail
reporteDetalle.summary: Everything needed to decide on a report: reason, reported content, history and who's handling it.
reporteDetalle.details: The detail gathers what you need to decide: the reason, the reported content, the history and who is handling it. Resolving records a decision; escalating hands the report to Popyplan when it's beyond the entity. The assignee is shown as 'a team member', not by name.
actions: Assign it to a team member
Escalate it to Popyplan if it's beyond the entity
tips: Read the history before deciding — previous moderation actions are part of the context.

guardia.title: On call
guardia.summary: Your entity's “I'm having a bad day” alerts and the settings for who's on call. Popyplan does not store phone numbers: contact happens through the app chat or through the referent.
guardia.details: Alerts are the app-side 'I'm having a bad day' requests from people in your entity. The on-call person — set by the owner — and the guardia see them even if their role isn't owner or moderator. Popyplan doesn't store phone numbers: contact happens through the app chat or the person's referent, and the panel shows whether someone from their support network has already stepped in.
actions: Set the help phone number and choose the on-call person (owner only)
See whether someone from the person's support network has already stepped in
tips: The on-call person sees this section even without a moderator role.
guardia.audience: Owner, moderator and whoever is on call.

informes.title: Reports & exports
informes.summary: Export the entity's metrics as CSV or PDF, by period and breakdown, ready to share with funders.
informes.details: Reports carry the same figures as the Home metrics for the chosen period — current month, last 3 or 12 months, or multi-year. A period can span at most 1461 days between the two dates. Any cell counting fewer than five distinct people shows as <5 — an aggregation threshold that protects privacy and cannot be turned off. The yearly breakdown groups the series by year instead of by month. Files only contain aggregates, never personal data.
actions: Choose the period and breakdown (regular or by year)
tips: Use the yearly breakdown for multi-year memory reports.
CSV opens in any spreadsheet; use PDF for a document to attach.

configuracion.title: Settings
configuracion.summary: The entity's details, team with their roles, and references between referents and people.
configuracion.details: Organization details, on-call settings, team and member references, and the entity's territorial scope. The team tab is owner-only: a moderator sees references and details but not the member list. Most writes here are audited and limited to the owner, so changes are traceable to whoever made them.
actions: Add or remove someone from the team (owner only)
Adjust the entity's details and colours
tips: Changing who is on call takes effect immediately for new help requests.
configuracion.audience: Owner and moderator; only the owner sees the team.

inicio.title: Umbrella home
inicio.summary: A single glance at the administration: the state of your declared territory and of the entities you fund, each with a link to its own section.
inicio.details: The umbrella home is the entry point to the two umbrella views: the territory observatory and the funded network. Both are aggregated dashboards governed by the same privacy rule as the rest of the panel — any group counting fewer than five distinct people shows as “<5” — and neither ever lists people. Open either view to change the period and explore the breakdowns.
tips: Everything here is aggregated: no individual person is ever identifiable.
inicio.audience: All roles of the umbrella entity.

territorio.title: Territory
territorio.summary: Everything happening in your declared territory's municipalities, whoever runs it: bubble map, table by municipality, monthly series and comparison with the previous period. Groups under five people show as “<5”.
territorio.details: The territory view aggregates every activity inside your declared scope, whoever runs it: an entity outside your network still counts if it works on your ground. The fixed schema and privacy threshold apply cell by cell — groups under five distinct people show as “<5”. The comparison measures the previous period of the same length and requires a breakdown. A municipality sheet shows only aggregates — never names of people or entities based there.
actions: Open a municipality to see its aggregated details
Compare districts, municipalities or provinces against the previous period
tips: The period can't span more than 1461 days (about 4 years).
A municipality sheet only shows aggregates: never names of people or entities.

informes.title: Umbrella reports & exports
informes.summary: Aggregated export of the territory or the funded network as CSV or PDF, with the same aggregation rules as the dashboards.
informes.details: Exports follow the same fixed schema and the same privacy threshold as the dashboards: groups under five distinct people export as “<5”, and no report ever contains people's names. Pick the scope — territory or funded network — the period and the breakdown, or “by year” for a multi-year record. PDF generation depends on the backend: when it isn't available you get a specific notice instead of a file, while CSV keeps working.
actions: Choose the scope (territory or funded network)
tips: “By year” gives one row per year and leaves the by-municipality section empty.
If PDF export is unavailable the notice says so explicitly; CSV still works.

redFinanciada.title: Funded network
redFinanciada.summary: Metrics for the entities under this administration — people, activities and attendance by municipality, entity and month, plus comparison with the previous period. It follows the parent/children tree, not the territory.
redFinanciada.details: The funded network aggregates the entities that hang off this administration, following the parent/children tree — an entity outside your territory still counts if it hangs off you. Each period loads the base cards plus the by-municipality, by-entity and monthly breakdowns, under the same threshold: groups under five distinct people show as “<5”. The comparison measures the previous period of the same length and requires a breakdown.
actions: Compare districts, entities or municipalities against the previous period
tips: The tree decides membership, not geography: children of your entities count even outside your territory.
People cells are suppressed under five; event counts are never suppressed.

inicio.title: Platform home
inicio.summary: Popyplan's overall status: verified and pending entities, escalated reports, unattended help alerts, contracts and invoices.
inicio.details: Each card opens its queue, and cards only appear for sections your role has: verified and pending entities, escalated reports, unattended help alerts, and — for roles that see Subscriptions — contracts and overdue invoices. The usage figures (active people, scheduled activities) come from an admin-only endpoint, so only superadmin gets them. A card that fails for any other reason reads “Not available” — a failure is never shown as a zero.
actions: Open each queue from its card
tips: Cards follow your role's menu: what you don't see is out of your role, not missing.
“Not available” means the request failed, not that the count is zero.
inicio.audience: Popyplan's team, according to their role.

entidades.title: Entities
entidades.summary: Every entity that has signed up, verified or not, with search and filters. Signing up and verifying are verifier and superadmin tasks.
entidades.details: The full directory of entities, verified or not. The list is paginated and filters by verification status and free-text search; the search applies shortly after you stop typing. Signing up a new entity is a verifier/superadmin action, and a new entity is born unverified until someone verifies it from its profile. Open a profile to manage its umbrella, scope, team, metrics and contract.
actions: Sign up a new entity (verifier and superadmin)
tips: New entities stay unverified until a verifier or superadmin verifies them.
The search box applies after a short pause while typing.

entidadFicha.title: Entity profile
entidadFicha.summary: An entity's details, umbrella, territorial scope, team, metrics, communities and contract, organised in tabs.
entidadFicha.details: Seven tabs in one profile: details (with verification), umbrella (reassigning the parent is superadmin only), territorial scope (superadmin from here; the entity's own titleholder can also widen it), team, metrics, communities and activities, and a read-only contract tab showing the active contract and its latest invoice. A verifier without a membership in that entity gets an explicit “No access” instead of fake data.
actions: Assign it an umbrella or extend its scope (superadmin)
tips: With several contracts, the tab prioritises the active one.
Reassigning the umbrella or widening the scope is superadmin-only from here.
entidadFicha.audience: Superadmin and verifier; some tabs are superadmin only.

reportes.title: Escalated reports
reportes.summary: Global queue of the reports that entities have escalated to Popyplan, with their entity and escalation date.
reportes.details: Only escalated reports reach this queue: an entity resolves what it can and escalates the rest to Popyplan. The list is not paginated — every escalated report is on one page — and names the originating entity, with an “Escalated” badge on those pending. Moderator and superadmin can assign and resolve; support has read-only access, so its action buttons are hidden rather than disabled.
actions: Assign or resolve it (moderator and superadmin); support can only view
tips: Only reports an entity escalated on purpose appear here; the rest stay in the entity's own queue.
Support sees the same queue with no action buttons.

reporteDetalle.title: Report detail
reporteDetalle.summary: Reason, content, originating entity and history of an escalated report.
reporteDetalle.details: The full picture of one escalated report: the reason in plain language, the reported content, the originating entity and its handling history. Moderator and superadmin can assign it to a team member or resolve it with a decision; for support every action is hidden, because its role is view-only. What the contract doesn't name is never invented — an assignment shows “a team member”, not an identity the data doesn't carry.
actions: Assign or resolve it (moderator and superadmin)
Review the reason, content and history (support reads the same view)
tips: Support's view is identical minus the actions: nothing is editable by mistake.
Reasons and statuses are translated; a value the panel doesn't know falls back to its raw text.

ayuda.title: Help alerts
ayuda.summary: “I'm having a bad day” alerts pending across the whole platform, to spot entities with no one on call to respond.
ayuda.details: One aggregated request lists every pending alert across all entities, so you can spot an entity whose alerts nobody answers. Each alert shows its entity, whether the person belongs to it, and their referent when they have one. Popyplan does not store phone numbers: contact happens through the app chat or via the referent. Handling an alert acknowledges it here and on the entity's own on-call screen at once.
actions: See the alert, its entity and its referent
tips: The fixed line under the list explains the no-phone rule — it isn't a missing field.
A badge marks alerts from someone who isn't a member of that entity.

verificaciones.title: Verifications
verificaciones.summary: Pending identity reviews: the person's evidence and the provider's reason, decided with a note.
verificaciones.details: The queue of pending identity reviews. Each row pairs the person's evidence (their appeal text) with the reason the provider flagged them, so you decide with both sides in view. Approving or rejecting always asks for a note, and the decision belongs to verifier and superadmin only. As you resolve reviews the queue shrinks; if the page you were on empties out, you return to the first one automatically.
actions: Approve or reject with a note
Review the person's evidence and the provider's reason first
tips: The note is part of the decision: write what a future auditor needs.
Resolved reviews leave the queue on their own; an emptied page returns you to the first one.

roles.title: Roles
roles.summary: Who makes up Popyplan's team and with which platform role.
roles.details: Platform roles are separate from entity roles: a person can be a platform admin and still hold a role inside an entity. Granting here gives access to the platform area only. Granting searches for the account by email or username; the user id always works as a fallback. Revoking is an explicit confirmation because it removes platform access immediately.
actions: Grant a role by searching for the account
tips: Revoking a role takes effect immediately.
The account search accepts email; the user id always works as a fallback.

auditoria.title: Audit log
auditoria.summary: Log of sensitive actions across the whole system, with filters by actor, action, target and dates.
auditoria.details: Every sensitive action across the system, superadmin only. Filters narrow by actor, action, target and date range, and each row renders its metadata as readable key=value pairs. The CSV export is a client-side download of the current page, not a server export: semicolon-separated with a BOM so Excel opens it correctly, every cell quoted, and values that could become spreadsheet formulas defused. Filter before exporting to get the slice you need.
actions: Export the current page to CSV
tips: CSV exports the current page only — filter first, then export.
Downloading a page is not itself audited; only backend actions are.

metricas.title: Metrics
metricas.summary: Aggregated metrics for the whole platform, by territory or by entity, with a comparison between periods.
metricas.details: Platform-wide metrics with the same fixed schema as entity metrics. The territory/entity selector decides which breakdown each request uses, and the comparison block is mandatory: you must pick a breakdown (province by default) to compare the current period with the previous one of the same length. Cells under 5 distinct people show as <5 — the privacy threshold applies at every scope.
tips: The yearly breakdown gives one row per year for multi-year views.

suscripciones.title: Subscriptions
suscripciones.summary: Popyplan's subscriptions with each entity: contracts, pricing tiers and invoices.
suscripciones.details: Three tabs: contracts, pricing tiers and invoices. Contracts move forward only — draft, active, ended — and invoices compute their own status (paid, pending, overdue). Only superadmin writes: for support the buttons are hidden, never disabled. And an ended contract is billing history alone — it never switches off any feature for the entity.
actions: Create and activate contracts, tiers and invoices (superadmin)
tips: Invoice status is calculated, not chosen: paying it (or its due date) moves it.
Ending a contract never affects what the entity can do in the panel.
suscripciones.audience: Superadmin and support; support can only view.

usuarios.title: Accounts
usuarios.summary: Every Popyplan account: search them, filter them and create a new one.
usuarios.details: This is account management, not managing an entity’s people: the email is visible here, but never documents or notes. The list goes from newest to oldest, 20 at a time, and the search looks at email, username, first and last name. The active/deactivated status does not come with each row: to see it, filter by “Status”. An account created here starts active and verified; platform access is not granted on creation but with a role in Roles.
tips: If you create an account without a password, send the password reset from its page afterwards.
Always open the account page from this list: that way it carries the account data.

usuarioFicha.title: Account details
usuarioFicha.summary: An account’s data, its public profile and the management actions.
usuarioFicha.details: The page brings together the account (email, username, join date, verification, platform role and entities) and its public profile (name, municipality, verification level). A suspended account has no public profile. Deactivating stops sign-in without losing anything and can be undone; deleting really removes the account and cannot be undone. Neither is offered on your own account. The password reset sends the person a code by email, in their language.
tips: When in doubt, deactivate: deleting cannot be undone.
The password reset shares the sign-in attempt limit: five per minute.

bloqueos.title: Blocks
bloqueos.summary: The blocks an account has made or received, and revoking them.
bloqueos.details: There is no list of every block: you look up those of one account, chosen with the search or from its page. Each row says who blocks whom by username and the date; a preventive block by phone number is shown without the number. Revoking undoes a block that belongs to someone else, so it asks for a mandatory reason, which is recorded in Audit.
actions: Revoke a block with a reason
tips: Only revoke with a clear reason: blocking is the person’s right.
The reason can be checked later in Audit.

actividades.title: Activities
actividades.summary: Look up Popyplan activities and cancel one if needed.
actividades.details: There is no list of all activities. By default you see the agenda: activities scheduled from today, open or from organisations you belong to. To see every activity of a community, past and cancelled included, search for it above or come from its record. Cancelling notifies people registered and on the waiting list, cannot be undone and is not recorded in Audit.
tips: Only cancel with a clear reason: people have already made plans.
For a past or cancelled activity, find it through its community.

chats.title: Chats
chats.summary: App conversations, for handling support cases.
chats.details: Lists active chat rooms, most recently updated first, 20 at a time. Search only looks at the room name, which one-to-one chats usually lack. Opening a conversation is support access: use it only when there is a reason, because the system does not record in Audit who reads it.
tips: Open a conversation only for a support reason.
To find a person, start from Users or Reports.

chatFicha.title: Conversation
chatFicha.summary: Read a conversation and reply as support.
chatFicha.details: Shows the participants and the messages, oldest first. Your replies go out under your own account and alias, not as “Popyplan”; the other person is only notified if the conversation is accepted and it does not arrive live if they have the chat open. The system does not record in Audit either the reading or the reply.
tips: Introduce yourself as Popyplan support when replying.
Never ask for or share phone numbers: the app does not store them.

comunidades.title: Communities
comunidades.summary: Every community on Popyplan, to search them and open their record.
comunidades.details: The platform sees every community: open, private, organisation-owned, both family spaces and deactivated ones. Only those of organisations you hid from your own account are missing. The list goes from newest to oldest, 20 at a time, and the search looks at name and description. Whether it is active only shows on the record.
tips: To deactivate, delete or moderate posts, open the record.

comunidadFicha.title: Community record
comunidadFicha.summary: A community's data, members and posts, with the moderation actions.
comunidadFicha.details: Deactivating hides the community in the app without deleting anything and can be undone; deleting really removes it, with its members, posts and chat. Members are managed as from the organisation: approve or reject requests, change roles and remove. A post can be hidden (undo with “Show”) or deleted for good. None of these actions is recorded in Audit.
tips: When in doubt, deactivate or hide: deleting cannot be undone.
As it is not recorded in Audit, note the reason for an important takedown elsewhere.

resenas.title: Reviews
resenas.summary: Every review people leave on activities, and deleting them.
resenas.details: The list brings every review, 20 at a time, newest first. Each row shows who wrote it, the 1-5 rating and the comment; the review does not carry the activity title. Deleting really removes the review, cannot be undone and is not recorded in Audit.
tips: Only delete reviews that break the rules: a bad rating is not a reason.

notificaciones.title: Notifications
notificaciones.summary: Send a notification to one person or to everyone, and manage the system templates.
notificaciones.details: A send to one person arrives at once; a send to everyone is queued and reaches every active account, staff included, with no final count. What is sent from here never uses templates and is not recorded in Audit. Templates only change the notifications the system itself generates for their type (if several of the same type are active, the oldest wins); their text is in English with placeholders in braces and is translated on the server.
actions: Send a notification to one person
tips: Before sending to everyone, test the text by sending it to yourself.
To stop using a template without losing it, deactivate it.

nomencladores.title: Catalogues
nomencladores.summary: The app's catalogues: languages, hobbies, community and activity categories, and training (disciplines, exercises and Popyplan templates).
nomencladores.details: Choose a catalogue and edit its items. Inactive ones, which the app no longer offers, are shown too. Deleting is final and sometimes cascades: a community or activity category takes its subcategories with it, and a hobby category with hobbies cannot be deleted. The server also rejects a repeated name within the same category. Community category images are not uploaded from here. Training: each discipline has a measure type (Strength, Endurance or Route); a discipline in use cannot be deleted (the server says so and it is deactivated instead). Names are edited in Spanish, Basque and Catalan. Only Popyplan templates are edited here, and saving a template replaces its whole list of exercises. The panel never shows anyone's workouts, routines or sports profile.
tips: When in doubt, deactivate instead of deleting.
The order decides how they are listed in the app.

tesoro.title: Treasure hunt
tesoro.summary: Marketing games organised by Popyplan: a slightly more complex activity, with clues and a prize.
tesoro.details: A game starts as a draft and is not visible in the app. When registration opens it is published in the agenda as an open activity, organised by whoever created the game, and whoever joins the game is registered in that activity. This version only supports individual, free games. Deleting a game also deletes its activity.
actions: See its status, participants and challenges
tips: Prepare the challenges and prizes before opening registration.
Mark as featured the game you want to promote in the app.

tesoroFicha.title: Game details
tesoroFicha.summary: A whole game in six tabs: details, challenges, prizes, participants, reviews and ranking.
tesoroFicha.details: The cycle always moves forward: draft → registration open → in play → finished. Starting needs at least one challenge and rejects pending requests. Answer challenges store the correct answer without ever showing it; location challenges check a radius in metres; photo and social challenges are reviewed by hand in Reviews. Prizes go by position bands that cannot overlap.
actions: Add, edit and delete challenges and prizes
tips: Rejecting a submission deletes it: the person can try again.
If you change the date of a finished game, it goes back to draft.

usuarioFicha.accountLoadError: The account data could not be loaded
usuarioFicha.accountNotFound: There is no account with this email and this id
usuarioFicha.noMemberships: Does not belong to any entity.
usuarioFicha.selfHint: This is your own account: you cannot deactivate or delete it from here.
usuarioFicha.passwordResetSent: A reset code has been sent to {email}.
usuarioFicha.deactivateDescription: The person will not be able to sign in to the app or the panel until you reactivate it. Their data is kept.
usuarioFicha.reactivateDescription: The person will be able to sign in again with their usual password.
usuarioFicha.deleteDescription: The account and everything that depends on it are deleted. This cannot be undone. If you only want to stop them signing in, deactivate it.

bloqueos.heading: Blocks
bloqueos.intro: Blocks between people for one account: the ones it made and the ones it received.
bloqueos.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin reviews blocks from the panel.
bloqueos.pickHint: Choose an account to see its blocks.
bloqueos.loadError: The blocks could not be loaded
bloqueos.revokeDescription: Both people will see each other again in the app. The reason is recorded in Audit.
bloqueos.reasonRequired: Write the reason for revoking it.

actividades.heading: Activities
actividades.intro: Popyplan activities: the public agenda or every activity of a given community.
actividades.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin reviews activities from the panel.
actividades.agendaHint: Agenda: only activities scheduled from today (or from “From”), open or from organisations you belong to. There is no list of all of them: to see past or cancelled ones, pick a community.
actividades.communityMode: Every activity of “{name}”, past and cancelled included.
actividades.communityModeUnnamed: Every activity of the chosen community, past and cancelled included.
actividades.cancelDescription: “{title}” is cancelled and everyone registered or on the waiting list is notified. It cannot be undone and is not recorded in Audit.

chats.heading: Chats
chats.intro: App conversations, for handling support cases.
chats.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin accesses chats from the panel.
chats.searchHint: Search only looks at the room name; one-to-one chats usually have none.

chatFicha.heading: Conversation
chatFicha.noticeTitle: Support access: open it only for a support reason.
chatFicha.noticeIdentity: Your replies appear under your own account and alias, not as “Popyplan”.
chatFicha.noticeDelivery: The other person is only notified if the conversation is accepted, and it does not arrive live if they have the chat open.
chatFicha.noticeAudit: The system does not record in Audit that you read the conversation or replied.
chatFicha.roomLoadError: The conversation could not be loaded
chatFicha.blockedHint: People your account has blocked, or who blocked you, are not shown.

comunidades.heading: Communities
comunidades.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin manages communities from the panel.
comunidades.listHint: All communities are listed, including private, organisation-owned, family-space and deactivated ones; communities of organisations you hid from your own account do not appear. Whether a community is active is shown on its record.

comunidadFicha.heading: Community record
comunidadFicha.notFound: This community does not exist or was deleted
comunidadFicha.loadError: The community could not be loaded
comunidadFicha.deactivateDescription: It stops showing in the app for its members and in discovery. Nothing is deleted: it can be reactivated.
comunidadFicha.reactivateDescription: It shows in the app again with its usual members and posts.
comunidadFicha.deleteDescription: “{name}” is deleted with its members, posts and chat. This cannot be undone. If you only want to hide it, deactivate it.
comunidadFicha.deletePostDescription: The post by {author} is deleted with its comments. This cannot be undone; to take it down without deleting it, hide it.

resenas.heading: Reviews
resenas.intro: Every activity review on Popyplan, newest first.
resenas.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin manages reviews from the panel.
resenas.deleteDescription: The review by {name} is deleted. This cannot be undone.

notificaciones.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin sends notifications and manages their templates.
notificaciones.heading: Notifications
notificaciones.intro: Send a notification to one person or to everyone, and manage the templates of system notifications.
notificaciones.sendHint: It reaches the app like any other notification (and by push or email if the person has it enabled). These sends never use templates: the text goes out as you write it. They are not recorded in Audit.
notificaciones.recipientNone: Choose an account with the search box.
notificaciones.targetAllHint: It will be sent to every active Popyplan account, platform staff included.
notificaciones.sentQueued: Bulk send queued: it will be delivered in the background.
notificaciones.sentTo: {count, plural, one {Sent to # person.} other {Sent to # people.}}
notificaciones.confirmAllDescription: The notification will reach every active Popyplan account, staff included. It cannot be undone or withdrawn afterwards.
notificaciones.confirmUserDescription: The notification will reach {name}. It cannot be withdrawn afterwards.
notificaciones.templateFormHint: Write the texts in English, with placeholders in braces ('{name}'): the system translates them into each person's language with the server catalogues and fills the placeholders with the notification data. Text that is not in those catalogues is sent as is.
notificaciones.templatesHint: A template only changes the notifications the system itself generates for that type; if several of the same type are active, the oldest is used. It never affects what is sent from the “Send” tab.
notificaciones.templatesLoadError: The templates could not be loaded
notificaciones.deleteDescription: “{name}” will be deleted. Notifications of that type will go back to their default text (or another active template of the same type). This cannot be undone.
notificaciones.activeHint: A new template starts inactive: once active, it immediately changes the text of every system notification of that type.

nomencladores.heading: Catalogues
nomencladores.intro: The catalogues used by the app and the panel: languages, hobbies, community and activity categories, and the training catalogue.

hints.languages: Languages a person can mark on their profile. The code is the two-letter ISO code and is unique.
hints.hobbyCategories: Groups of profile hobbies. The code is unique.
hints.hobbies: Hobbies a person can mark on their profile, each in its category. The code is unique.
hints.communityCategories: Community categories. The name is unique. The category image is not uploaded from the panel: editing here keeps the current one.
hints.communitySubcategories: Community subcategories, each in its category. Do not repeat a name within the same category.
hints.eventCategories: Activity categories, with their type and an icon (an emoji or short text).
hints.eventSubcategories: Activity subcategories, each in its category. Do not repeat a name within the same category.

deleteWarnings.languages: The language is deleted. Profiles that had it keep the code, which will no longer be shown. If you only want to stop offering it, deactivate it.
deleteWarnings.hobbyCategories: A category with hobbies cannot be deleted: delete its hobbies first or, better, deactivate it.
deleteWarnings.hobbies: The hobby is deleted. Profiles that had it keep the code, which will no longer be shown. If you only want to stop offering it, deactivate it.
deleteWarnings.communityCategories: All its subcategories are deleted too, and communities using it are left without a category. This cannot be undone; if in doubt, deactivate it.
deleteWarnings.communitySubcategories: The subcategory is deleted and removed from the communities that had it. This cannot be undone.
deleteWarnings.eventCategories: All its subcategories are deleted too, and activities using it are left without a category. This cannot be undone; if in doubt, deactivate it.
deleteWarnings.eventSubcategories: The subcategory is deleted and removed from the activities that had it. This cannot be undone.

nomencladores.loadError: The catalogue could not be loaded

hints.disciplines: Each sport and how it is measured: Strength (exercises with sets, reps and weight), Endurance (duration and distance) or Route (distance, elevation and duration). A discipline in use cannot be deleted: deactivate it.
hints.exercises: Exercises of each discipline. The metric decides the shape of each set: weight and reps, reps, time or distance. The code is unique.
hints.templates: Popyplan templates that the app offers to log a workout quickly. Only Popyplan templates are shown here: the panel never shows anyone's workouts, routines or sports profile.

training.disciplinesLoadError: The disciplines could not be loaded.

deleteWarnings.discipline: A discipline with exercises, templates or workouts cannot be deleted: deactivate it instead.
deleteWarnings.exercise: The exercise is removed from the catalogue. Templates and workouts that used it keep its name as a free exercise.
deleteWarnings.template: The Popyplan template is deleted and the app stops offering it. Workouts logged with it do not change.

tesoro.heading: Treasure hunt
tesoro.intro: Games organised by Popyplan. When registration opens, each game is published in the agenda as an open activity.
tesoro.noAccessDescription: Only superadmin manages the treasure hunt.
tesoro.loadError: The games could not be loaded
tesoro.emptyHint: Create the first one with «New game»: it starts as a draft and is not published until registration opens.
tesoro.deleteDescription: «{name}» will be deleted with its challenges, prizes and participants, and also its agenda activity if it was already published. This cannot be undone.

form.name: Name
form.startInPast: The start has to be a future date.
form.maxParticipantsHint: Empty = no limit. It is also the capacity of the published activity.
